item.title: Lewis Hamilton says he could win record eighth F1 championship as Ferrari’s number one driver
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has suggested that a record-breaking eighth world title would have been within reach this season had Ferrari chosen to prioritise him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. His comments came after he collided with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, an incident described as "completely unacceptable" by Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur . Stewards later penalised Leclerc for his role in the collision. Following his first victory for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona , Hamilton moved 40 points ahead of Leclerc and sat 41 points adrift of Antonelli. Although the 41-year-old rejected claims he asked Ferrari to make him their lead driver, he suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have given Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Charles Leclerc collided with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass to win in Las Vegas “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy throws a pass Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. (Fernando Llano/Associated Press) MEXICO CITY – On Sunday night, a year after Brock Purdy joined teammate George Kittle for a youth clinic in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback returned to the country to take a very menacing group of grown men to school. The NFL's "Mexico City Game" quickly became the Brock Purdy Game in a game against an opponent that was supposed to slow his league-MVP roll. The Vikings arrived with the NFL's top-scoring defense, a blitz-crazed unit led by mad scientist coordinator Brian Flores and Purdy drove Minnesota mad and crazy in a 35-10 romp at Estadio Banorte. The late-game chants from the raucous, pro-49ers crowd of 85,612: "MVP, MVP, MVP!" "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. That is correct, Kyle. Minnesota arrived allowing 14 points a game. Purdy capped two of the first three drives with touchdown passes of 17 and 8 yards to Kittle and the 49ers had 14 points in 15-plus minutes. The Vikings had allowed three passing touchdowns in their previous 27 quarters. Purdy had three scoring tosses with 2:14 left before halftime. "Best player in the game right now," wide receiver Mike Evans said. It's safe to say this: Purdy is the best quarterback Minnesota has seen this season. Purdy completed 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns, posting a 146.0 QB rating. The Vikings had allowed an NFL-low 69.5 rating entering Sunday that Purdy more than doubled. The highest rating against them in the first nine games: Detroit's Jared Goff (88.1). "I thought every time I looked up, he was peppering completions," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said. "Total poise. Command." The Vikings' blitz-heavy scheme specializes in making QBs harried. On Sunday, however, Purdy completed 17 of 19 passes for 208 yards with two touchdowns when Minnesota sent five or more rushers, which it did on 20 of his 26 dropbacks, according to ESPN. Purdy's completion percentage (89.5) against pressure was the highest the Vikings had allowed since 2016. "Oh my gosh," Kittle said, "he was so good." A sampling of some of Purdy's greatest hits? item.title: Real Madrid yet to make final decision about Nico Paz -report
item.description: Real Madrid are still monitoring Nico Paz’s performances with Como but have not made a final decision about whether or not the club will trigger their €80 million option to buy him back next summer, according to a report published today on AS. At Valdebebas, views regarding the Tenerife native remain unchanged. Indeed, doubts concerning a potential return have not dissipated. Club officials are acutely aware that the player seeks playing time and a prominent role, and at present, his prospective arrival would entail competing primarily with players such as Jude Bellingham or Arda Güler, with Brahim Díaz and Rodrygo also awaiting their opportunities. There is no indication whatsoever of a possible change of heart. Source: AS The same can be said about Franco Mastantuono and Jacobo Ramón, per that same report. It would be much cheaper for Madrid to bring them back but Los Blancos will keep monitoring the situation until next summer.

item.title: VIDEO: Gary Neville slaps himself in the face TWICE during bizarre rant as Manchester United nightmare continues against Liverpool
item.description: Manchester United v Newcastle United - Carabao Cup Final - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville reached his breaking point on live television as he watched his former club Manchester United crumble during a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. The legendary full-back left fellow pundits stunned after resorting to physical outbursts to express his sheer disbelief at the defensive display. Red card and defensive collapse spark studio outburst Mauricio Pochettino's tenure at Manchester United suffered a miserable blow as Liverpool ran riot at Anfield. The visitors' plans unravelled inside 10 minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for hauling down Alexander Isak after Matthijs de Ligt lost his positioning. A starting backline featuring Yoro, De Ligt, and Lisandro Martinez struggled against relentless attacks. Even introducing Harry Maguire failed to halt the onslaught as Liverpool exposed a defence weakened by another summer of neglect. Watching from the Sky Sports studio, Neville reached boiling point during the post-match debrief. His bizarre rant left Jamie Carragher laughing and drew amusement from the broadcast panel. Watch the clip Dissecting the collapse on Sky Sports, the former United captain took aim at the defenders' poor body language. He claimed the backline never looks alert during matches. "I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head)," Neville said. "I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…" Bruh! Man United players have traumatised Gary Neville. He is literally slapping himself on Sky Sports 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/b1uiOLEf3t — Jaja (@JajaBreed) November 22, 2026 Neville stared blankly for several seconds. He then slapped his own face twice while saying "wake up" each time, before finishing: "You play for Man Utd!" Defensive crisis leaves Pochettino in relegation trouble The loss leaves United in the relegation zone with just one win from 11 Premier League matches. They have also conceded more goals than any side across Europe's top five leagues. Neville was especially critical of Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt following a year-long injury layoff. However, the pundit acknowledged how tough it is to return after a year on the sidelines. "I have a lot of sympathy for him," Neville added. "It’s like playing football after having six pints. It’s a strange feeling. I have a lot of sympathy for him, it’s alarming to watch." Urgent defensive rebuild awaits Pochettino Pochettino faces an immediate battle to lift United out of the drop zone and build on a solitary league win from 11 outings. Fixing the leakiest defence in Europe's top five divisions will be his top priority. Carefully managing De Ligt's fitness after a year out will be crucial. Without rapid improvements at the back, United risk sinking deeper into a relegation fight.

item.title: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams
item.description: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams Bayern stumbled and Dortmund pounced, yet Bremen’s buoyant display in the Nordderby was the major talking point from this Bundesliga weekend. Spearheaded by Niclas Füllkrug, Die Grün-Weißen now find themselves in sixth position. It is a welcome change from last season’s relegation fight: a challenge overcome under Daniel Thioune, who recently signed a deserved contract extension. Quite rightly, Füllkrug’s ten goals from the same number of matches occupy the headlines. However, it is worth noting that Marco Grüll has made a significant contribution in finding the net twice and assisting on six separate occasions. With the prolific German striker providing a much-needed focal point, Justin Njinmah’s pace now poses even more danger to opposing backlines. Hamburg found out the hard way, as the dynamic winger struck twice in Sunday’s four-goal rout. It never ceases to amaze how much of a difference one summer can make. Karl Hein made his place between the sticks permanent, racking up two domestic clean sheets since. Matters further up the pitch have aligned with Chuki and Eren Dinkçi, both anchored by fellow new face Ludovit Reis. Austrian centre-back and long-serving club captain Marco Friedl also remains a constant presence. Hoffenheim and Leipzig have even fallen short at the Weserstadion, one of few remaining fortresses during this campaign. Four wins and a single draw – the latter coming against newly promoted Paderborn – put the team second on home form alone. Sitting in the European places despite injury setbacks makes this feat even more impressive. Jens Stage will be out until the new year, while Felix Agu is recovering from a calf issue. Mitchell Weiser came back from a lengthy spell on the sidelines, only to immediately experience a thigh problem in late October. Kicking off the next round of fixtures on Friday offers another opportunity to build on this progress and extend what can now affectionately be called the ‘Bremen bounce’ as a struggling Borussia Mönchengladbach come to town. Locked in their own fight for survival, the visitors will be hoping to show the same resilience as their hosts did not that long ago. With a firing Füllkrug in their midst, few would bet against the men in green and white impressing once again in front of such energetic support.

item.title: Pio Esposito devastated despite historic Inter hat-trick as Cristian Chivu's men throw away points in eight-goal Atalanta thriller
item.description: Atalanta BC v FC Internazionale - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter striker Pio Esposito struggled to hide his disappointment despite etching his name into the Nerazzurri record books during a chaotic Sunday night in Bergamo. The young forward became the first Italian to net a hat-trick for the club since the legendary Christian Vieri, yet his heroics were overshadowed by a defensive collapse. Nerazzurri collapse in Bergamo thriller Inter’s visit to the New Balance Arena on Monday night turned into a bruising encounter that exposed the fragile nature of their current defensive setup. Despite holding the lead on multiple occasions, Cristian Chivu’s side allowed the hosts to claw back into the game, eventually settling for a point in a dramatic eight-goal stalemate . The result left a bitter taste in the mouth of the visitors, who had appeared to be in total control for large periods of the match. "It is difficult to explain a result like this," a dejected Esposito told Sky Sport Italia . "We never managed to kill the game off definitively, and therefore something did not go well. In the end, we conceded four goals. It is not just about the defense; we must refine all the details together and we will sit down to analyze the problems we faced." Esposito matches Vieri record While the team result was disappointing, Esposito’s individual performance etched his name into the Inter history books. By scoring three times, he became the first Italian player to record a hat-trick for the club since Bobo Vieri. It was a display of clinical finishing that demonstrated why he is considered one of the brightest prospects in the national team setup, showing a predatory instinct that rarely gave the Atalanta backline a moment of peace. Reflecting on the milestone, the striker remained grounded, stating: "It's a beautiful thing but today I am finding it hard to enjoy it because we let two points be pulled away from us and my first thought is that we didn't manage to take the three points home. I hope that the best Pio isn't now, but day by day, and above all I hope that the goals can lead to victories." The forward targets consistency Esposito’s rise continues to be one of the few silver linings for the club during a period of inconsistency. His tally for the season continues to grow, placing him among the top Italian scorers in the division alongside the likes of Alphadjo Cisse and Antonio Raimondo. However, the player himself insists that personal accolades mean little if the team cannot find a way to stabilize their defensive performances in high-pressure situations. "In the heat of the moment, I really struggle to give an explanation," Esposito added. "We manage to create many chances and support the action well, but then we must be capable of maintaining the result and not allowing these matches to be reopened. item.description: SPRINGFIELD —The world of college athletics is seeing young people profit from their play. Name, Image, and Likeness has taken over. While some athletes are receiving a flat check, others are using their marketing prowess to build brands and businesses. Enter Kaemyn Bekemeier, Missouri State’s star guard. item.title: Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender
item.description: Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton races ahead of team mate Charles Leclerc during the Las Vegas Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Lewis Hamilton believes he could have won a record eighth Formula One world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritized him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton’s claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix – a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as “completely unacceptable.” Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision. Hamilton’s maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc. And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him their number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

item.title: Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany (R) speaks with Jamal Musiala during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut») Tom Weller/dpa Germany sporting director Rudi Völler believes Bayern Munich should wait to see how Jamal Musiala progresses before discussing his contract situation, as the club toned down their rhetoric and a top lawyer said a wage cut was all but impossible. Germany and Bayern playmaker Musiala has been affected by absence seizures, a form of epilepsy, this season and the Bundesliga champions have openly wondered whether he will ever be the same player again. Honorary president Uli Hoeness spoke of a dilemma for the club, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family. Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge also questioned the 23-year-old's lucrative contract signed just last year. "One should wait a bit," Völler told broadcaster Sky Germany late on Sunday. "He is playing. It is not as if he cannot play right now. Bayern need him for the next few weeks." Musiala, one of Bayern's top earners until 2030, missed the start of the season due to his neurological condition and then picked up a hamstring injury. He returned off the bench in the 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday and almost bagged a winner. Bayern are massively stretched following long-term injuries to key forwards such as Harry Kane, meaning Musiala will be needed more than ever in the coming weeks as they try to catch up with new leaders Borussia Dortmund. "I hope, as we all do ..., that it will be the way it was before," Völler remarked. "I am optimistic about that. He showed it before, even though he had the illness. We need Jamal in the national team too. He has shown what an exceptional player he is." At a visit to a fan club in the Bavarian town on Kronach on Sunday, Dreesen was more conciliatory. "We are giving Jamal time, and we have to do that," he said, according to Münchner Merkur/tz newspaper group. "It is like in your own company when someone is no longer able to do everything. That is a new situation in football, one we have to learn to deal with," he added. Addressing a fan who had asked a question, Dreesen said: "Your message is: speak, but speak a bit more quietly. I think everyone has understood that." Bayern have been widely criticized across the game for talking publicly about a possible contract renegotiation or wage cut. Leading German sports lawyer Joachim Rain told RTL that Bayern would have little chance of doing so legally. "A unilateral adjustment of the salary is not an option. Termination would only be conceivable in the event of permanent inability to play. There are currently no indications of this. Musiala is not permanently unable to work," he said.

item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the Formula 1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer. The announcement of Rafael Camara as Bearman's 2027 team-mate, which came ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, was expected to be swiftly followed by that of his British team-mate. Instead, the silence has dragged on to the point of becoming a talking point, even prompting rumours of Bearman driving elsewhere next year. The paradox is that Bearman and Haas have strong reasons to reach an agreement. Bearman has ruled out racing elsewhere in 2027, while Haas has long been expected to retain him, yet the negotiations have dragged on far longer than initially anticipated. In recent weeks, there has been speculation about the reasons for the deadlock, some linked to the contractual relationship between Bearman and Ferrari and to the future prospects of the 21-year-old Briton. According to information obtained by Motorsport.com, however, the issue holding up the signing does not concern the driver’s long-term future, but rather the financial terms of the deal with Haas. Ferrari has already exercised the option allowing it to retain Bearman within its driver programme. Given that Maranello has invested financial resources in the young Briton ever since he joined the Driver Academy in 2021, allowing Bearman to leave on a free transfer would be a big waste of all those efforts. Rafael Camara will finish the 2026 season for Haas as he prepares for his full 2027 debut alongside Oliver Bearman. The Scuderia has not ruled out any of its longer-term options. The immediate negotiations therefore centre on two parties: Haas and Bearman’s entourage. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
